text:
The Edmonton Oilers are 17-6-4 and have lost four straight (0-3-1), outscored 20-12, after Vegas beat them 5-3 on Tuesday. Both facts matter, and the second one is closer to the truth about this team.

The headlines are about two stars making history. NHL.com wrote that Connor McDavid's bid for a 200-point season is drawing raves from Wayne Gretzky, Leon Draisaitl just passed 1,100 career points, and Evan Bouchard has been chasing a Paul Coffey streak. When McDavid and Draisaitl play together with Vasily Podkolzin, Edmonton takes 60% of the expected goals and has outscored opponents 22-8.

The rest of the roster is the worry. Over the season the Oilers have only 49% of the expected goals, and they've scored about 26 more goals than their chances deserve. During this skid they've had just 44% of the expected goals, so the losses aren't bad bounces. The Mathieu Joseph, Alex Formenton and Owen Michaels line gets 31%, and the Connor Murphy and Ryan Shea pair 42%.

Mike Babcock's first season still projects to about 103 points and a 96% playoff chance, because the banked points are real. Tristan Jarry has been the steadying hand in net (.925 over his last five starts) after Devon Levi had a rough week. Friday is the next test of whether the depth can hold its own minutes.
headline: The Oilers' record is ahead of their hockey
